The semiclassical measures of parabolic matrices on T${}^2$ are explicitly characterized by proving that they have at most three nonzero Fourier coefficients in position. A partial quantum ergodicity statement for parabolic matrices is obtained by proving a sharp bound on the quantum variance and some examples are built in higher dimensions. In particular, starting from T___ there always exist semiclassical measures whose projection on the position has only nonzero Fourier coefficients. Moreover, if Q is isotropic over the rationals, then there exist semiclassical measures whose projection on the position concentrate on some subtori. A link is made with the semiclassical measures of the Laplacian on the torus.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Ferrari-Dominguez (IRMA)

item.title: Simultaneous Sharp-Interface Limits for a Diffuse-Interface Landau--de Gennes Droplet Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.26440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nematic droplet models based on diffuse interfaces involve competing microscopic transition layers whose interaction is lost if the small parameters are sent to zero successively. We study this interaction for the diffuse-interface Landau--de Gennes model of Shi et al., with phase-field thickness $\varepsilon$ and exterior $Q$-tensor relaxation length $\kappa_\varepsilon$, and show that their relative scale selects the effective sharp-interface theory. Within a regular-interface class, we establish the corresponding sharp-interface limit for every limiting ratio $r=\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}\kappa/\varepsilon\in[0,+\infty]$. Three qualitatively different regimes emerge. When $r=+\infty$, the two transition layers separate asymptotically and the interfacial costs decouple, recovering the previously obtained iterated limit. When $r\in(0,+\infty)$, the layers overlap and produce a genuinely coupled, $r$-dependent anisotropic surface density. When $r=0$, finite energy forces the interior trace of $Q$ to vanish on the limiting interface. The comparable-scale regime requires a genuinely coupled interfacial analysis. Thus the exterior relaxation length is not merely a regularization parameter: together with the phase-field thickness, it determines the macroscopic surface energy and anchoring law of the sharp-interface limit.
item.dc:creator: Sisi Guan, Wei Wang, Lei Zhang

item.title: Wiener's criterion and resolutivity for the $p$-parabolic equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.26466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize boundary regularity for $u_t=\Delta_p u$ in arbitrary bounded open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ for $n\ge2$ and $p\in(2n/(n+1),2)\cup (2,\infty)$. We prove equivalent Wiener criteria in terms of capacitary potentials on prescribed cylinders and in terms of intrinsic capacities. Both require divergence at every positive obstacle height. Independently, we prove Perron resolutivity for continuous data on the full topological boundary of every nonempty bounded open set for all $n\geq 1$ and $p>1$. As an application of the Wiener criterion, we prove a Petrovski\u{\i}-type criterion in the singular range, which gives regularity of the origin for $|x|<C(-t)^{1/p}$ for every $C>0$. For $2<p<n$, examples show that divergence at every sufficiently large height does not imply regularity.
item.dc:creator: Benny Avelin, Mikko Parviainen

item.title: A direct obstacle proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ bound for the Gaussian Riesz transforms
item.description: arXiv:2610.26478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a detailed, direct proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ estimate for the first-order Gaussian vector Riesz transform, using the fractional obstacle method of Ouyang, Spector, and Stockdale. For $d\gamma_n=\pi^{-n/2}e^{-|x|^2}\,dx$, let $L=-\tfrac12\Delta+x\cdot\nabla$, $D=2^{-1/2}\nabla$, and $R_\gamma=DL^{-1/2}\Pi_0$, where $\Pi_0$ removes the mean. We prove that $R_\gamma$ has weak-type constant at most $2$ on real-valued inputs, independently of $n$. The main construction is the unique unshifted decomposition $F=g+L^{1/2}u$, for nonnegative $F\in L^2(\gamma_n)$ and $a>\int F\,d\gamma_n$, with $u\geq0$, $\min\{F,a\}\leq g\leq a$, preservation of mass, and $g=a$ on $\{u>0\}$. We retain the details of coercivity, the Lewy--Stampacchia estimate, the upgrade from the form domain to the operator domain, and locality. We also identify the $L^1$ extension with the principal-value transform and obtain the constant $8/\pi$ for complex-valued inputs.
item.dc:creator: Cristian E. Guti\'errez, Juan Manfredi

item.title: Well--posedness and homogenization of a waste--protein clearance model in cortical tissue
item.description: arXiv:2610.26498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate and analyze a mathematical model for the clearance of waste proteins from cortical tissue. The model tracks three species of waste proteins, distinguished by their size, and incorporates constant production at neuronal surfaces, reaction-diffusion in the bulk of interstitial fluid, and nonlinear dynamics on capillary surfaces. We establish the existence, boundedness, and uniqueness of a solution to the microscopic model. Using two-scale convergence, we derive a homogenized model and prove that the microscopic solutions converge to the corresponding macroscopic limit. The resulting model reveals how the microscopic arrangement and relative volume fractions of neurons and capillaries affect waste-protein transport and clearance at the tissue scale. Numerical simulations illustrate these effects and demonstrate how variations in cortical microstructure translate into differences in the macroscopic clearance dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Miroslav Bul\'i\v{c}ek, Ansgar J\"{u}ngel, Marie E. Rognes, Lucie Wintrov\'{a}

item.title: Blow-up bounds under profile approximation for superconformal wave equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.26513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the focusing semilinear wave equation in the superconformal, Sobolev-subcritical range, we prove an upper blow-up bound at the ODE rate near a non-characteristic point, assuming approximation by signed multiples of explicit stationary profiles in similarity variables. The comparison parameters may vary with time, and the error is measured only in a degenerate energy norm on a small extension of the unit ball. The main step is a quantitative exclusion of concentration at the boundary of the profile family. It follows from the nonnegativity of the superconformal Hamza--Zaag energy at admissible vertices and an upper perturbation estimate. We also exclude families with an isolated dominant profile and, under a noncancellation condition, clusters of comparable profiles. For the latter, we derive a limiting energy in $\R^{N+1}$ which accounts for the interactions between profiles.
item.dc:creator: Firas Kaabi

item.title: Narrow escape problems beyond spherical holes: slits and tubes
item.description: arXiv:2610.26514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The narrow escape problem consists in characterizing the exit event of a Brownian motion trapped inside a domain with reflecting boundary and small absorbing holes.Using recent advances in the quasi-stationary distribution approach, we first give an explicit set of hypotheses that allows one to derive the asymptotics of the exit time and of the exit hole distribution. We then apply it in dimension three to several hole shapes: spherical holes, thin spheroidal holes shrinking to curves on the boundary (slits), and holes located at the end of thin tubes attached to the domain. We illustrate the accuracy of the results with numerical simulations, and extend them to higher dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Louis Carillo

item.title: The Israel-Stewart equations with a physical vacuum boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.26533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish local existence for the nonlinear Israel--Stewart equations describing a relativistic viscous fluid with a physical vacuum free boundary. Compared with ideal fluids with a physical vacuum, the relaxation equation for the bulk viscosity introduces further derivative loss. The problem is compounded by the degenerate nature of the equations of motion on the free boundary. In this work, we construct solutions in weighted Sobolev spaces via a Nash--Moser iteration. Since the domain moves, the iteration is carried out in Lagrangian coordinates, while the linearized operator at each iterate is inverted on the Eulerian domain with the local well-posedness of the linearized equations established in our earlier work.
item.dc:creator: Runzhang Zhong

item.title: Global strong solutions to the aligned 2.5D non-resistive full MHD system with high temperature and a strong magnetic field
item.description: arXiv:2610.26547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for an aligned vertical-field reduction of the full compressible non-resistive MHD equations in two space variables. The shear and bulk viscosities are proportional to $\theta^\alpha$, and the heat conductivity is proportional to $\theta^\beta$. For $2<\alpha<\beta<\alpha+2$, we prove global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions when the background temperature and the comparable magnetic background are sufficiently large, while the positive density background is fixed. The velocity and temperature perturbations belong initially to $H^2$, and the transported magnetic perturbation belongs to $H^1\cap D^{1,4}$; their absolute norms may be bounded by an arbitrary fixed constant. Alignment is essential and implies a small density perturbation relative to the magnetic background. Our proof combines relative energy estimates, uniform in the background temperature and magnetic field, with coupled estimates for the material derivatives of the velocity and temperature. These bounds control the source terms in the damped magnetic-gradient equation, allowing us to close the global a priori estimates without a separate large-time decay assumption. We construct the global strong solution by smooth approximation and Sobolev energy estimates for the approximating solutions, and prove uniqueness by an energy estimate for the difference of two solutions.
item.dc:creator: Yachun Li, Zixuan Qu, Zhaoyang Shang

item.title: On sharp stability of the BCC quantizer
item.description: arXiv:2610.26553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove sharp nonlinear stability estimates for the squared-distance quantization energy of the body-centered cubic lattice. The reference Hessian has optimal coercivity constant \(1/96\) relative to nearest-neighbor displacement differences, uniformly over all finite-index periods. We classify all equality modes and prove cubic cancellation on their span. This yields nonlinear stability in a neighborhood independent of the period, including volume-preserving strain. The loss in the sharp energy coefficient is at most quadratic for each fixed period and exactly linear when all periods are allowed. We also determine the transition between these regimes. Finally, we prove global optimality and uniqueness of BCC, up to rigid motions, among two-site configurations with rectangular period cells of fixed volume.
item.dc:creator: Senping Luo, Bingbing Xie

item.title: Vorticity growth beyond bounded relative vorticity for axisymmetric Euler flows without swirl
item.description: arXiv:2610.26559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish upper bounds for vorticity and related quantities in axisymmetric Euler flows without swirl in $\mathbb{R}^3$, assuming that the initial relative vorticity $\omega_0/r$ belongs to $L^1\cap L^p$ with $3<p\le \infty$. For each fixed $p \in (3,\infty]$, we obtain polynomial-in-time upper bounds for the radial moments, the radial velocity, and the $L^p$ norm of vorticity. We then consider initial data with unbounded relative vorticity whose growth near the axis is controlled by $\Phi (\log \tfrac{1}{r})$ for a subexponential profile $\Phi$, so that $\omega_0/r$ belongs to $L^p$ for every $p<\infty$ but not to $L^{\infty}$. For such data, we derive profile dependent upper bounds for the vorticity maximum. In particular, for any polynomial function $\Phi (s)=s^k$ with $k\ge 0$, we show that $\|\omega (\cdot,t)\|_{L^{\infty}}$ is bounded by $(1+t)^{\frac{4}{3}+k} (\log (2+t) )^{\frac{2k}{3}}$. Moreover, for initial data satisfying $\omega_0/r \in L^1\cap L^p$ with a fixed $p\in (3,\infty)$, under additional symmetry and vertical confinement assumptions, we obtain a subexponential-in-time upper bound for the vorticity maximum, thereby improving the classical exponential bound for such data.
item.dc:creator: Khakim Egamberganov

item.title: General Periodic Conservation Laws Motivated by Traffic Modeling
item.description: arXiv:2610.26574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper deals with the well-posedness, in the spatially periodic setting, of a mixed system of nonlocal-local conservation laws modeling traffic flow where autonomous vehicles --- informed on traffic conditions over long distances --- interact with human-driven bulk traffic. We also provide a comprehensive well-posedness theory in the periodic framework separately for general local conservation laws and for systems of nonlocal conservation laws, together with a priori total variation bounds and stability estimates.
item.dc:creator: Rinaldo M. Colombo, Mauro Garavello, Claudia Nocita

item.title: Pointwise Wave--Damping for Linearized Vlasov--Poisson: Compactly Supported Radial Equilibria and Relativistic Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.26600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish weighted pointwise estimates for the response Green function and the complete electric field of the linearized Vlasov--Poisson system in $\mathbb{R}_x^3\times\mathbb{R}_v^3$ around compactly supported radial equilibria. Both decompose into a dispersive wave component with $t^{-3/2}$ decay in $L_x^\infty$ and a faster-decaying Landau-damped component. The wave estimate includes the survival threshold, where the oscillatory branch meets the continuous spectrum, while the damped estimates resolve the spatial fronts associated with the velocity boundaries. The equilibrium class includes shells with independent inner and outer orders of vanishing, down to first order, and profiles positive throughout a velocity ball. The proof combines a joint treatment of pole and continuum contributions with a low-frequency normal form for the electric field. The electric-field estimates hold for real, neutral perturbations with finite weighted regularity and imply uniform scattering along free characteristics. An exact momentum--velocity correspondence for suitable filled-ball profiles yields analogous estimates and scattering for a class of nonnegative relativistic equilibria with polynomial momentum tails.
item.dc:creator: Haina Li, Quoc-Hung Nguyen, Zhilong Xue

item.title: A new localization approach for Willmore flows: Asymptotic analysis for the Dirichlet problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.26602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Willmore flow with Dirichlet boundary conditions by means of a new geometric localization approach. In contrast to previous works, we do not rely on localized energy estimates, but on uniformly controlled isothermal coordinates and localized parabolic a priori estimates. For genus-zero surfaces satisfying an explicit energy condition depending only on the prescribed boundary data, we prove global existence together with a dichotomy between smooth convergence and subconvergence to a complete noncompact Willmore surface. If the initial Willmore energy is at most $4\pi$, this dichotomy reduces to smooth convergence after reparametrization, and we show that this additional threshold is optimal. As an application, we obtain an existence criterion for the stationary Dirichlet Willmore problem.
item.dc:creator: Simon Blatt, Manuel Schlierf

item.title: Weighted potential and Green systems with Dini coefficients and primitive growth
item.description: arXiv:2610.26656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a nonexistence theorem for positive potential systems with continuous coefficients satisfying distributional Euler lower bounds and a uniform Dini modulus on normalized logarithmic dilations. The nonlinearities have positive lower logarithmic derivatives and positive primitive-to-endpoint ratios. The common radial kernel is comparable with a Riesz kernel. A localized transport identity, a primitive pressure estimate and implicit amplitude normalization give uniform local energy bounds and a dilation contradiction. And we treats the genuine Green kernel of $-\Delta+V$ for nonnegative potentials under annular and Newton composition budgets and a strict gap corrected by the relative Green dilation defect. Relative endpoint differences and an exact virtual-energy cancellation retain local nonlinear energy as the only initial energy hypothesis. Independent representation arguments give these consequences, including even integer orders without initial tails. A compact family of normalized responses also yields universal interior bounds without regular variation.
item.dc:creator: Hongtao Hu, Zhouyu Long, Wenming Zou

item.title: Improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri Inequalities under Constraints: Sharpness and Quantitative Remainders
item.description: arXiv:2610.26691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequalities on the sphere under moment constraints, with particular emphasis on sharp leading constants and quantitative remainder terms. For the Sobolev inequality, we sharpen the almost sharp inequality of Hang and Wang [30] (Int. Math. Res. Not., 2022) to a sharp one at $p=2$ under vanishing moment constraints of orders $m=1,2,3$. We also prove a general failure principle: if the unconstrained sharp Sobolev inequality fails, then the corresponding sharp improved inequality under moment constraints fails as well. For the Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequality, we sharpen the almost sharp inequalities of Chang and Hang [10] and Hang [29] (Comm. Pure Appl. Math., 2022) to a sharp improved inequality at the critical order $s=\frac{n}{2}$ under arbitrary finite-order moment constraints. We further investigate the best remainder constant. In contrast with the two-dimensional first-moment case of Gui and Moradifam [28] (Invent. Math., 2018), where the best remainder vanishes, we show that it is positive in several higher-dimensional regimes. We also obtain quantitative remainder estimates for general almost sharp improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequalities, which in turn yield sharp inequalities at different scales. We further extend recent second-moment refinements to higher dimensions and higher orders. Finally, we obtain analogous results on sharpness, non-sharpness, and quantitative remainder estimates for improved Sobolev-type inequalities under symmetry constraints on general smooth closed manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Zhou, Wenming Zou

item.title: Logarithmic corrections and interacting fronts in shifting environments and competition systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.26702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate refined large-time propagation and front interaction in a two-species Lotka--Volterra competition--diffusion system on the real line. When the faster competitor spreads into unoccupied habitat, its invasion front generates a moving heterogeneous environment for the trailing competitor, whose front position may be influenced by the leading front's Bramson delay. We first study a scalar Fisher--KPP equation in a shifting environment. Under weighted integrability assumptions on the growth profile, we determine the logarithmic front corrections up to a bounded error and identify the corresponding limiting wave profiles, thereby explicitly demonstrating how the logarithmic displacement of the environment modifies the classical Bramson correction. The resulting asymptotics distinguish locally pulled propagation, nonlocal pulling, and two critical transition regimes. In the forced-wave regime, the invasion front remains locked to the moving environment, and the dynamics select a unique stationary profile from a one-parameter family. In the nonlocal pulling regime, the favourable habitat ahead accelerates the invasion front even though the front lags behind the environmental shift. At the threshold of nonlocal pulling, the interaction modifies only the logarithmic correction and, at a further critical parameter value, produces an additional $\ln\ln t$ term. We then apply these results to the competition system. In the nonlocally pulled regime, we determine the logarithmic displacement of the trailing invasion front, explicitly quantifying the transmission of the leading species' Bramson delay, and prove convergence to the corresponding travelling-wave profile. Finally, we establish a Liouville-type rigidity principle for a class of monotone parabolic systems. This yields uniqueness of monostable travelling waves in both competition regimes.
item.dc:creator: \'Emeric Bouin, King-Yeung Lam, Chang-Hong Wu

item.title: An Inverse Problem for the Moore Gibson Thompson Equation: Injectivity and Stability
item.description: arXiv:2610.26760v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an inverse problem for the variable coefficient Moore Gibson Thompson (MGT) equation in a bounded domain, where the objective is to recover an unknown initial acceleration from boundary measurements of the acoustic field. We establish both injectivity and stability of the associated measurement operator. Injectivity is established through a unique continuation property by applying a theorem of Tataru for analytically principally normal operators. The argument relies on a factorization of the third order operator into wave type components, combined with Carleman estimates and propagation techniques in the spirit of Tataru. Stability is derived through a microlocal analysis of the forward operator, based on the construction of geometric optics approximate solutions and the identification of an elliptic pseudodifferential operator arising from microlocal back propagation of the data. These results connect the MGT inverse problem with the classical theory of hyperbolic inverse problems, such as photoacoustic tomography, while highlighting new features induced by the third order dynamics and damping.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Rodriguez, Benjamin Palacios

item.title: Singular Aubry--Mather Sets for a Homogeneous Single-Input Control System
item.description: arXiv:2610.24145v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop an Aubry--Mather theory for the abnormal arcs of a time-minimal single-input affine control system in dimension three with homogeneous cubic drift. We show that the Bonnard--Kupka semi-invariant defining the abnormal locus is a Darboux polynomial of the desingularized singular field, with an explicit cofactor; this gives the invariance of the abnormal locus, a closed formula for the multiplier of its periodic components and, through the antipodal symmetry of the model, their description as lifts of ovals of a real plane quintic. For a compact invariant set of a singular flow we then define a singular Aubry--Mather structure, whose Lagrangian is supported on the graph of the singular field and whose Hamilton--Jacobi equation is linear in the momentum. We prove a duality formula for the critical value, the existence of critical subsolutions strict outside the Aubry set, and the covariance of the structure under time changes. On the abnormal locus the structure selects the periodic components of minimal average cost, governs transverse stability, and exhibits a sharp obstruction to correctors along heteroclinic cycles; for the radial exponent of the homogeneous dynamics, the corrector is the periodic part of the logarithmic radius. An explicit cubic example illustrates the results.
item.dc:creator: Bernard Bonnard, Cristian Mendico

item.title: A counterexample to the local existence of conformal normal metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.24541v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every dimension $n\ge3$, we construct a smooth Riemannian metric whose entire Taylor series at a point agrees with the Euclidean metric and whose conformal class contains no smooth conformal normal metric near that point. For the metric used in the construction, parametrized by a smooth angular function, we prove that conformal normalization forces a dimension-dependent exponential decay rate for the spherical harmonic components of that function. This gives counterexamples whenever the angular coefficients decay too slowly. In particular, every nonanalytic angular function yields a counterexample. The proof combines a weighted cylinder estimate with an integral identity relating the angular spectral coefficients of the background volume defect to the nonlinear remainder. We also give a direct counterexample to the linear right inverse used in Cao's smooth existence argument and identify the failure of angular summability in that construction.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Zhang

item.title: Index-one capillary minimal hypersurfaces in \(\mathbb R^n_+\)
item.description: arXiv:2610.24878v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify complete, two-sided, properly embedded capillary minimal surfaces with nonempty boundary and Morse index one in \(\mathbb R^3_+\). More precisely, if the boundary is compact, these surfaces are catenoid truncations; if the boundary is noncompact, they are capillary hairpin surfaces. The classification extends to higher dimensions under extrinsic Euclidean volume growth and Wang--Zhang's dimension and angle conditions.
item.dc:creator: Chenghang Lu

item.title: LowNet: Looped Wavelet Neural Networks with 24 Learnable Parameters for Solving Poisson Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.24941v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Poisson equations frequently appear in various fields, such as mathematics, physics and informatics. Solving Poisson equation, however, is challenging. Traditional methods are not data-specific, although have high certainty. They require a large number of iterations due to the CFL numerical stability. In contrast, deep learning methods are data-driven and more efficient, but require accurate training data and suffer from heavy computation. To tackle these issues, we propose a wavelet-inspired Poisson solver with 24 trainable scalars. The proposed network has several advantages. First, it is compact. It has four independent $5\times5$ kernels, each represented by six parameters, leading to 24 scalars in total. Such compact format can be deployed on most devices. Second, thanks to the loop design, it achieves higher accuracy than previous methods. A residual loop reuses the wavelet block without increasing its parameters. Numerical experiments confirm that such loop indeed improves the solving accuracy. On 10000 images, one, two, and three loops of the wavelet block lead to PSNRs of $47.27$, $74.14$, and $100.74$ dB, respectively. Third, the proposed method is computationally fast. Thanks to the wavelet transform, the proposed method has linear computation complexity, leading to high computation performance. In short, we propose a novel looped wavelet neural network with compactness, accuracy and efficiency for solving Poisson equations. Our method can be applied in various fields, such as computational fluid dynamics, image reconstruction, biomedical engineering, electromagnetic field simulation.
item.dc:creator: Yuanhao Gong

item.title: Pseudodifferential structure, rigidity, and sharpness for the Steklov problem on differential forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.25000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We resolve four questions concerning Karpukhin's Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator on differential forms. First, for $0\leq p\leq n-2$, we prove that the operator is classical pseudodifferential of order one and compute its principal symbol, which is elliptic on the coclosed symbol space. This answers Open Question 7.19 in the survey of Colbois, Girouard, Gordon, and Sher [7]. Second, the symbol calculation yields a Weyl law with remainder $O(\tau^{n-2})$, resolving the smooth case of their Open Question 7.23 in [7]. Third, in the critical dimension $n=2p+2$, we show that conformal deformations of the Euclidean ball fixing the boundary metric preserve the full operator. Nonisometric metrics therefore retain all equalities in Karpukhin's initial equality range, disproving the isometry-rigidity assertion of Conjecture 2.12 in [19](the rigidity assertion of Conjecture 7.27 in [7]). Fourth, we establish the all-index sharpness asserted in Conjecture 2.13 in [19](the sharpness assertion of Conjecture 7.27 in [7]) in the class of smooth compact connected oriented Riemannian manifolds with boundary. For $p\geq1$, a shrinking-core construction inspired by the collapsing models of Ann\'e and Takahashi produces manifolds with fixed spherical boundary and explicit two-sided bounds for an initial eigenvalue cluster.
item.dc:creator: Daguang Chen, Guotao Huang, Tingyu Liao

item.title: Semi-classical Szeg\H{o} kernel asymptotics on CR manifolds of high codimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.25255v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we consider a CR manifold $X$ of high codimension and a CR line bundle $L$ over $X$. For each $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $L^k$ denote the $k$-th power of $L$. We establish that the spectral projection $\Pi_{k,\leq k\mu_k} := \mathbf{1}_{(-\infty, k\mu_k]}(\Box_{b,k})$ converges to the weighted Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the sense of distributions, where $\Box_{b,k}$ denotes the Kohn Laplacian with values in $L^k$. Moreover, when $\Box_{b,k}$ possesses a local spectral gap, we show that the Szeg\H{o} projection $\Pi_k$ converges to the weighted Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the sense of distributions. We also provide an explicit formula for the Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group. Furthermore, we consider a high codimension CR manifold $X$ equipped with a transversal and CR $\mathbb{R}^m$-action. In this setting, we prove that the partial Szeg\H{o} projection $\Pi_{k,({\mathbb R}^m\curvearrowright,\leq k\delta)}$ converges to the weighted partial Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the $\mathcal{C}^\infty$ topology. As an application of our results, we establish a Kodaira embedding theorem for high codimension CR manifolds with a transversal and CR $\mathbb{R}^m$-action.
item.dc:creator: Chin-Yu Hsiao, Chin Jui Yang

item.title: Observability of wave equations with time- and space-dependent potentials: a counterexample under GCC and a positive criterion on the disk
item.description: arXiv:2610.25327v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the geometric control condition (GCC) for the free wave equation does not guarantee internal observability in the presence of a smooth time-dependent potential. On a bounded connected domain with analytic boundary, we construct a nonempty open observation set such that the pair satisfies GCC and the free Dirichlet wave is observable, and a smooth $2\pi$-periodic potential for which there exists a nonzero smooth Dirichlet wave that vanishes on the observed cylinder for all time. The wave is the unique mild solution in the space $X_\Omega=L^2(\Omega)\times H^{-1}(\Omega)$ on every finite interval, so no finite observation horizon yields an observability inequality for this fixed potential. The construction starts from a real-valued local counterexample to unique continuation across a noncharacteristic hyperplane; this local statement is of independent interest, since earlier constructions for the wave operator use complex-valued waves and potentials. The global counterexample is obtained by joining flat oscillatory solutions along the edges of a polygonal observation set, repairing their sum at the vertices without changing its zero set, and then using a spatial transition to a common time-independent pair near the boundary. For comparison, on the unit disk we show that an observation region containing a central disk and a neighborhood of an embedded cross-cut yields observability for every weak wave at sufficiently large observation time, with constants uniform over bounded measurable potentials; the proof uses a cut, logarithmic polar coordinates, and a Carleman weight whose favorable flux is confined to the observed artificial boundary.
item.dc:creator: Zhonghua Liao, Qi L\"u, Xu Zhang

item.title: Endpoint capacity at strictly stable minimal boundaries:Gaussian layers and Schwarzschild deficits
item.description: arXiv:2610.25444v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(M^n,\mathfrak g)$, $3\le n\le7$, be a one-ended asymptotically flat manifold whose boundary $\Sigma$ is a connected, strictly stable, outermost minimal hypersurface. As $p\downarrow1$, the $p$-capacity of $\Sigma$ converges to its area, by a theorem of Fogagnolo and Mazzieri. We establish a higher-order asymptotic expansion governed by a single function on $\Sigma$: the positive solution $g$ of the reciprocal Jacobi equation $Jg=g^{-1}$. After a universal term, the first correction is determined by the average of $\log g$, and the capacitary potential drops from one to zero across a Gaussian boundary layer of width $g\sqrt{p-1}$; under the normalized energy measure, the logarithm of the gradient has limiting variance $\frac12$ plus the variance of $\log g$. In dimension three, assuming in addition that $R_{\mathfrak g}+|\mathrm{II}|^2\ge0$ along $\Sigma$, we identify the capacity deficit of $\Sigma$ relative to the Schwarzschild horizon of the same area at order $p-1$: it is nonnegative, vanishes exactly when the induced metric of $\Sigma$ is round and $R_{\mathfrak g}+|\mathrm{II}|^2\equiv0$, and controls the deviation of $g$ from a constant through a relative-entropy identity.
item.dc:creator: Sehong Park

item.title: Tensorial pinching by deforming curvature cones in higher codimension mean curvature flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.25610v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a pinching method for mean curvature flow in higher codimension. Motivated by pinching constructions for Ricci flow, the method uses a nonlinear deformation of the second fundamental form. We introduce two tensorial curvature conditions for closed immersions in Euclidean space which extend beyond the scope of classical scalar pinching results. In dimensions at least ten, we apply the method to prove convergence to a round point under the first condition and a canonical neighborhood theorem under the second.
item.dc:creator: Tsz-Kiu Aaron Chow

item.title: Convergence of alternating score-system iterations for regularized Landau particle dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.25780v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyze an alternating iteration for score-based particle approximations of the homogeneous Landau equation. Each step computes a regularized score along the previous trajectory and recomputes the trajectory with that score frozen. First, at fixed positive regularization, we prove existence, uniqueness, and $W_1$-Lipschitz stability of a Tikhonov score minimizer in a vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert space embedded in $C_b^2$. For bounded Lipschitz collision matrices, this yields factorial convergence to the coupled regularized dynamics on every finite interval, with constants independent of particle number. Global objective gaps and system residuals control inexact solves, and structural kernel assumptions ensure momentum and energy conservation. The mean-field and alternating-iteration limits commute at fixed regularization in this regime. Second, score-difference cancellation extends the theory to far-field-truncated Landau kernels with $\gamma \geq -2$ and the uncut case $\gamma=-2$. For the uncut three-dimensional Coulomb kernel, a separate continuum construction gives local factorial convergence from bounded, compactly supported densities. Third, we characterize the obstruction to removing regularization at fixed particle number and establish a separate conditional density-level convergence criterion under uniform regularity and approximation assumptions, using relative entropy. A heat-equation counterexample shows that an unregularized density-level Picard iteration can diverge. Atomic Coulomb and simultaneous particle-zero-regularization limits remain open.
item.dc:creator: Yeoneung Kim, Donghyun Lee, Sung-Jun Son

item.title: Quantitative stratification and optimal regularity for stationary $J$-holomorphic maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.25813v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we give an alternate proof of the $\epsilon$-regularity theorem of Wang [Comm. Cont. Math. 2003] for weakly $J$-holomorphic maps by adapting the conservation law approach of Rivi\`ere [Invent. Math. 2007]. Then we adapt the powerful quantitative stratification method of Naber--Valtorta [Ann. Math. 2017] to obtain optimal volume estimates and rectifiability for the quantitative strata of stationary $J$-holomorphic maps. In contrast with general harmonic maps, the almost complex equation gives rise to an additional symmetry improvement: Every odd-dimensional translation symmetry extends to an even-dimensional one. Consequently, consecutive even and odd strata coincide, and the $k$-th quantitative stratum satisfies a tubular-neighborhood estimate with exponent $2m-2\lfloor k/2\rfloor$, where $2m$ is the real dimension of the domain. The corresponding strata are $2\lfloor k/2\rfloor$-rectifiable, with almost-everywhere unique complex planes of symmetry. Finally, we prove that every stationary $J$-holomorphic map is smooth if the target { manifold} admits no non-constant $J$-holomorphic sphere, improving the corresponding theorem of Wang.
item.dc:creator: Chang-Yu Guo, Ming-Lun Liu, Chang-You Wang

item.title: The $(n-2)$-linear restriction estimate in $\mathbb R^n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.25907v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a proof for the $(n-2)$-linear extension estimate for curved surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge5$, at the local product exponent $2(n-1)/(n-2)^2$, with an arbitrarily small power loss. The hypotheses are transversality of the normals and nondegeneracy of the compressed shape operators on their common two-dimensional orthogonal complement. The argument combines polynomial partitioning, a descent through algebraic varieties, localized multilinear restriction, and positive packet-energy estimates.
item.dc:creator: Faruk Temur

item.title: Quadratic growth rigidity for the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.26016v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation on $\mathbb{C}^{n}$, we prove the Liouville theorem for solutions with quadratic growth.
item.dc:creator: Jianchun Chu, Yaxiong Liu

item.title: Cutoff beyond non-negative curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.26019v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how a relaxed gradient estimate is enough to prove cutoff for several new families of Markov processes, within the varentropy framework of [Sal25]. In particular, we show how certain regularization estimates from hypocoercivity theory allow one to prove cutoff for kinetic dynamics. Moreover, we prove cutoff for some families of diffusions with non-convex potentials and for mean-field dynamics, as well as for biased random walks on the symmetric group, giving a simple proof of a far-reaching extension of a result of [NY24].
item.dc:creator: Max Fathi, Arnaud Guillin, Cyril Labb\'e, Justin Salez

item.title: Two-dimensional semilinear stochastic heat equations with critical long-range correlations
item.description: arXiv:2610.26249v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a $(2+1)$-dimensional semilinear stochastic heat equation in which the noise is correlated like $f(\log |z|)/|z|^2$ as $|z|\to \infty$. Under an appropriate rescaling and logarithmic attenuation, we show that the limiting two-point statistics are given by the solution to a forward-backward stochastic differential equation. As shown in the work of Cosco, Cottini, and Donadini (2025), with whose results our study agrees in the linear case, the interesting feature of the two-dimensional, long-range problem is that one sees a varying influence on the limiting distribution from a range of spatial scales. We show that this phenomenon appears in the decoupling function for the limiting object and that the function $f$ modulates the weight of the contribution of each spatial scale.
item.dc:creator: Bryan Castillo, Alexander Dunlap

item.title: Young Parabolic PDEs and the Martingale Problem for Young SDEs
item.description: arXiv:2610.26291v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Under mild regularity assumptions, we prove that the martingale problem associated with the hybrid Young--Lyons--It\^o differential equation admits a unique solution in the natural class of solutions satisfying Krylov-type estimates, thereby establishing probabilistic weak well-posedness. Our proof relies on an analysis of the associated Kolmogorov equations, which are Young-type parabolic PDEs with irregular coefficients. The resulting theory for such Young-type parabolic PDEs is also of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Bugini, Michele Coghi, Khoa L\^e, Chengcheng Ling

item.title: Outer trapped surface formation from gravitational waves collision
item.description: arXiv:2610.26320v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a new rigorous construction of outer trapped surface formation in smooth vacuum spacetimes without symmetry assumptions. The outer trapped surface is produced by the collision of two transversely localized, nearly plane-fronted gravitational waves described by short pulse data. The outer trapped surface is obtained by joining two smooth pieces along a curve with their future-directed outer null normals matching continuously. The incompleteness of the maximal future development is then established by adapting Penrose's original argument. This construction is inspired by Penrose's argument in constructing a marginally outer trapped surface in the collision of two ultra-relativistic particles modeled by the Aichelburg--Sexl solution.
item.dc:creator: Junbin Li

item.title: Average lower bound on magnetic double-well tunneling with asymptotically large well separation
item.description: arXiv:2610.26637v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study tunneling between two identical, smooth, compactly supported potential wells in a constant perpendicular magnetic field, with the coupling and magnetic field fixed and the well separation tending to infinity. For a sufficiently small positive magnetic field, we prove lower bounds on the hopping coefficient and on the splitting of the two lowest eigenvalues outside a set of separations of density zero. If the well centers are separated by $2d_1$ and the magnetic field strength is $b\lambda$, the lower bounds have the form $e^{-b\lambda d_1^2-Cd_1^{1+\delta}}$ for every fixed $\delta\in(0,1)$. No radial or reflection symmetry of the single-well potential is assumed. The proof combines the explicit Landau resolvent kernel with a complex analytic estimate for logarithmic averages of the hopping coefficient.
item.dc:creator: Charles L. Fefferman, Say-Yeon Kwon, Jacob Shapiro, Michael I. Weinstein

item.title: Weak solutions for weak turbulence models in electrostatic plasmas
item.description: arXiv:2304.12430v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The weak turbulence model, also known as the quasilinear theory in plasma physics, has been a cornerstone in modeling resonant particle-wave interactions in plasmas. Stemming from the Vlasov-Poisson/Maxwell system under the weak turbulence assumption, incorporating the random phase approximation and ergodicity, it takes the form of a integro-differential system, which describes the time dynamics of particle distribution and wave spectrum. The interaction between particles and waves can be treated as a stochastic process, whose transition probability bridges the momentum space and the spectral space. To our knowledge, there is no preceding rigorous analytical work for the quasilinear theory addressed in this manuscript. In this paper, we establish the existence of global weak solutions to the one-dimensional electrostatic quasilinear model for nonnegative, smooth, rapidly decaying initial particle distributions and nonnegative, smooth wave spectra compactly supported in a positive wave-number band. The construction uses the resonance condition to reduce the coupled system to a scalar degenerate parabolic equation, together with uniform estimates and strong convergence of the gradients of regularized approximations. When the initial wave spectrum is positive throughout a single band, we further characterize the equilibrium selected by this approximation procedure. The equilibrium uniquely minimizes a quadratic functional over a nonnegative cone and admits a geometric construction through the least concave majorant of a primitive determined by the initial data. The limiting particle distribution is non-increasing on the corresponding resonant interval and forms plateaus wherever the equilibrium auxiliary function is positive. A relative-entropy argument establishes long-time convergence to this equilibrium.
item.dc:creator: Kun Huang, Irene M. Gamba

item.title: Singular semilinear elliptic equations in half-spaces
item.description: arXiv:2409.00365v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the monotonicity of positive solutions to the problem $-\Delta u = f(u)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N_+ := \{(x',x_N)\in\mathbb{R}^N \mid x_N>0 \}$ under zero Dirichlet boundary condition with a possible singular nonlinearity $f$. In some situations, we can derive a precise estimate on the blow-up rate of $\frac{\partial u}{\partial\eta}$ as $x_N \to 0^+$, where $(\eta,e_N)>0$, and obtain a classification result. The main tools we use are the method of moving planes and the sliding method.
item.dc:creator: Phuong Le

item.title: A P\"oschl--Teller approximation to the wave equation outside a torus
item.description: arXiv:2505.15264v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove dispersive estimates for an approximation to the wave equation in the exterior of a torus. Because no separation of variables into a basis of eigenfunctions and eigenvalues exists in toroidal coordinates for the time harmonic problem, we introduce a related approximate operator for the Dirichlet Laplacian in the exterior of a torus. The approximate operator separates into Schr\"odinger operators with P\"oschl-Teller potentials after freezing $N=N_0$ in the conjugated Laplacian. The operator here which we develop is related to the so-called Mehler-Fock kernel. Using the known solution to the eigenvector and eigenvalue problem of P\"oschl-Teller, a high-frequency analysis of the approximate operator for the wave equation can be made accurately. The operator for this problem gives an angularly truncated $L^1\rightarrow L^{\infty}$ dispersive estimate on compact coordinate collars. Duhamel's principle controls its error for the corresponding exterior wave operator with Dirichlet Laplacian.
item.dc:creator: Ronald Quirchmayr, Alden Waters

item.title: Boundary estimates for singular elliptic problems involving a gradient term
item.description: arXiv:2508.07360v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study bounded positive weak solutions of the singular quasilinear problem $-\Delta_p u+\vartheta|\nabla u|^q=u^{-\gamma}+f(u)$ in a bounded $C^2$ domain, with zero Dirichlet boundary data, where $p>1$, $\gamma>0$, $0<q\le p$, $\vartheta\ge0$, and $f$ is continuous up to zero and locally Lipschitz on $(0,\infty)$. We establish sharp boundary asymptotics for the solution and its directional derivatives. For $\gamma>1$ the leading profile is a universal power of the boundary distance; for $\gamma=1$ it is logarithmic, with the sharp constant $(p/(p-1))^{1/p}$. In both cases the normalized gradient converges uniformly to the inward normal multiplied by the corresponding constant. For $0<\gamma<1$ we prove global $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity and a classical Hopf boundary estimate. We also obtain the optimal Sobolev integrability threshold and the sharp logarithmic modulus of continuity. Finally, positivity of the total source on the solution range yields symmetry and monotonicity in symmetric domains strictly convex in one direction; when $N\ge2$ and $\vartheta>0$, we assume $q\ge\max\{1,p/2\}$.
item.dc:creator: Phuong Le

item.title: Well-Posedness of Fully Nonlinear PDEs on Star-Shaped Networks with Nonlinear Kirchhoff Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2510.14364v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The aim of this paper is to establish the well-posedness of fully nonlinear partial differential equations on star-shaped networks subject to nonlinear Kirchhoff conditions at the junction. The branchwise operators may be discontinuous across the junction, and uniform ellipticity is required only in a neighborhood of the vertex. Our approach relies on the construction of auxiliary test functions solving suitable nonlinear ordinary differential equations, whose structure allows us to control the viscosity inequalities at the junction. We first show that generalized Kirchhoff viscosity solutions in the sense of Lions-Souganidis satisfy the strong Kirchhoff condition. Combining these auxiliary functions with an affine perturbation of supersolutions and precise junction gradient estimates, we establish a comparison principle for bounded semicontinuous viscosity sub- and supersolutions. Existence and uniqueness are then addressed through Perron's method and the comparison principle. Finally, we discuss first-order junction problems and a possible transmission condition arising from vanishing viscosity.
item.dc:creator: Isaac Ohavi

item.title: Energy minimizers in a periodic phase transition model of light-matter interaction in nematic liquid crystals
item.description: arXiv:2510.17291v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we complete the study of global minimizers of a forced, non autonomous, one dimensional, phase transition model, initiated in [8]. Motivated by the recent findings in [9], revealing new configurations of topological structures in light, we consider a forcing term having two periods. We show that depending on the strength of the forcing, at most two thresholds that determine the structure of the minimizers (kinks) are attained. These kinks are now a combination of three types observed experimentally, and they may have at most three zeros. The existence of these complex types of phase transition follows from a periodic one dimensional model of matter-light interaction in nematic liquid crystal based on a thin sample limit of the Oseen-Frank energy. We show that the qualitative behaviour of global minimizers is consistent with the original model.
item.dc:creator: Panayotis Smyrnelis, Marcel G. Clerc, Manuel Diaz-Zuniga, Micha{\l} Kowalczyk

item.title: Multiplicity of bound states for a class of nonlinear Dirac equations on generalized star graphs with potentials
item.description: arXiv:2511.09285v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we investigate the existence and multiplicity of bound states for a class of nonlinear Dirac equations on a generalized star graph \(\mathcal{G}\): \[ -ic\,\sigma_1\,\partial_xu+mc^2\sigma_3u+V(x)u=f(|u|)u,\qquad x\in\mathcal{G}, \] where \(V:\mathcal{G}\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous, \(f\in C^1([0,\infty))\), \(m>0\), \(c>0\), and \(\sigma_1,\sigma_3\) are the Pauli matrices. Under suitable monotonicity and growth assumptions on \(f\), a uniform spectral gap and sufficiently long constant-potential intervals on \(k\) terminal edges yield at least \(2^k-1\) bound states, distinct up to a constant phase. The constant potentials on these intervals may differ. The construction uses half-line solutions and a uniform inverse estimate. For potentials tending to a constant at infinity, we prove compactness below the full-line ground level. In the flat-well setting, the solutions localized near individual terminal vertices lie below this level and provide a ground state through the generalized Nehari minimization. In particular, one localized solution is obtained for each minimum component containing a long terminal interval.
item.dc:creator: Guangze Gu, Ziwei Li, Michael Ruzhansky, Zhipeng Yang

item.title: Fully localised three-dimensional solitary water waves on Beltrami flows with strong surface tension
item.description: arXiv:2511.16843v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fully localised three-dimensional solitary waves are steady water waves which are evanescent in every horizontal direction. This paper presents an existence theory for such waves under the assumptions that the relative vorticity and velocity fields are parallel (`Beltrami flows'), that the free surface of the water takes the form $\{z=\eta(x,y)\}$ for some function $\eta: {\mathbb R}^2\rightarrow{\mathbb R}$, and that the influence of surface tension is sufficiently strong. The governing equations are formulated as a single equation for $\eta$, which is then reduced to a perturbation of the KP-I equation. This equation has recently been shown to have a family of nondegenerate localised solutions, and an application of a suitable variant of the implicit-function theorem shows that they persist under perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Mark D. Groves, Erik Wahl\'en

item.title: Feedback Stabilization and Tracking for Heat Equations Using Thermo-Plasmonic Nanoparticles as Actuators
item.description: arXiv:2602.14581v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a feedback strategy to track prescribed heat profiles using plasmonic nanoparticles as actuators. Starting from a thermo--plasmonic Maxwell--heat model, we use a time-domain discrete effective description in which the generated heat is approximated by a superposition of heat kernels centered at particle locations with amplitudes governed by a coupled Volterra system. We recast this dynamics as a heat equation on a bounded domain with finitely many point actuators and design a tracking feedback based on pointwise evaluations of $\mathcal A^{-1}y$, where $\mathcal A=I-A_0$ and $A_0$ is the Neumann diffusion operator. Working in the natural $V'$ setting with $V=D(\mathcal A)$, we prove exponential stabilization of the tracking error via distribution-actuator theory. For non-equilibrium reference profiles, we add a constant feedforward term and a low-mode fixed-point pre-compensation on $X_N$, ensuring exact steady matching on $X_N$ and an explicit bound on the residual tail mismatch.
item.dc:creator: Arpan Mukherjee, S\'ergio S. Rodrigues, Mourad Sini

item.title: Schr\"odinger ultrahyperbolic equations with singular coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2603.03170v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we investigate the Cauchy problem for Schr\"odinger ultrahyperbolic equations with singular (less than continuous) coefficients. We prove $H^\infty$ well-posedness in the very weak sense under suitable assumptions of the distributional structure of the coefficients and decay on the lower order terms. Consistency is proven with the classical $H^\infty$-results when the equation coefficients are smooth.
item.dc:creator: Claudia Garetto, Davide Tramontana

item.title: Sublinear elliptic equations with a sharp change of sign in the nonlinearity
item.description: arXiv:2603.11766v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the semilinear indefinite elliptic problem \[ -\Delta u = Q_\Omega |u|^{p-2}u \quad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^N, \] where $Q_\Omega = \chi_\Omega - \chi_{\mathbb{R}^N \setminus \Omega}$, $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ is a bounded smooth subset, $N \geq 3$, and $1 \leq p < 2$, with $p=1$ corresponding to the sign nonlinearity. Using a variational approach, we investigate the uniqueness or multiplicity of nonnegative solutions depending on the shape of $\Omega$ and the existence of different types of nodal solutions. We also show that all solutions have compact support and analyze how the support of the ground state depends on $p$, proving convergence to the whole space as $p\to 2^{-}$ and identifying some qualitative features such as starshapedness and Lipschitz regularity of the support. We also establish a link between these problems and a two-phase Serrin-type torsion overdetermined problem.
item.dc:creator: M\'onica Clapp, Alberto Salda\~na, Delia Schiera

item.title: Zonal states and improved $L^\infty$ bounds for eigenfunctions of magnetic Laplacians on hyperbolic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2603.12177v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish polynomially improved $L^\infty$ bounds for eigenfunctions of magnetic Laplacians on hyperbolic surfaces in the critical energy regime. We also show that, below the critical energy, the H\"ormander bound is saturated by explicit eigenstates, which we call magnetic zonal states. These states resemble zonal harmonics on the sphere and equidistribute on Lagrangian tori in phase space.
item.dc:creator: Ambre Chabert, Thibault Lefeuvre

item.title: Optimal $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity up to the boundary for fully nonlinear elliptic equations with double phase degeneracy
item.description: arXiv:2604.04776v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we establish optimal $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity up to the boundary for viscosity solutions of fully nonlinear elliptic equations with double phase degeneracy law and oblique boundary conditions. The approach developed here relies on first deriving uniform boundary H\"older estimates for perturbed models with oblique boundary data in ``almost $C^{1}$-flat'' domains. Building upon these estimates, the desired regularity is obtained through a compactness and stability framework for viscosity solutions. As a byproduct of our analysis, we determine the optimal H\"older exponent for solutions when the governing operator is quasiconvex or quasiconcave. In addition, we establish an improved regularity result along vanishing points of the source term.
item.dc:creator: Junior da Silva Bessa, Jehan Oh

item.title: Asymptotic stability of Landau solutions to the MHD system and energy decay
item.description: arXiv:2604.15910v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the three-dimensional incompressible MHD system. Any weak solution satisfying a strong energy inequality is $L^2$-asymptotically stable around a Landau solution. Under an additional integrability assumption on the initial perturbation, we also obtain an explicit algebraic decay rate for the $L^2$-norm of the velocity and magnetic perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Nicola De Nitti, Yun Wang, Shaoheng Zhang

item.title: Magnetic uncertainty in variable geometry
item.description: arXiv:2604.20794v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study Hardy-type uncertainty principles and unique continuation properties for linear covariant Schrodinger equations with variable coefficients in the presence of bounded electric and magnetic potentials. Under suitable smallness assumptions on the leading coefficients, we prove that any solution exhibiting super-quadratic exponential decay at two distinct times must vanish identically. Under an additional structural assumption on the coefficient matrix $G$, we further establish a Hardy-type result at the quadratic exponential scale. We also obtain an analogous uniqueness result for the heat equation with variable-coefficient magnetic perturbations. Our results unify and extend previous works in two directions: they recover the constant-coefficient covariant case treated by Barcelo-Fanelli-Gutierrez-Ruiz-Vilela when $G=I$, and the variable-coefficient non-magnetic case considered by Federico-Li-Yu when $A=0$. The proofs combine logarithmic convexity arguments with Carleman estimates adapted to variable-coefficient covariant Schr\"odinger and parabolic flows. Although our approach follows the general strategy introduced by Escauriaza-Kenig-Ponce-Vega, substantial new difficulties arise from the interaction between the variable metric and the magnetic structure, which requires new weight functions and refined commutator estimates.
item.dc:creator: Luca Fanelli, Yilin Song, Ying Wang, Jiqiang Zheng, Ruihan Zhou

item.title: Solutions to Monge-Amp\`ere Equations with Low Codimensional singularities
item.description: arXiv:2605.19142v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct solutions to Monge-Amp\`ere equations whose Monge-Amp\`ere measures contain singular components supported on low codimensional sets. We also study the regularity of such solutions. To motivate our construction, we present examples arising from optimal transport where the potential of optimal transport maps satisfy Monge-Amp\`ere equations similar to the ones we study.
item.dc:creator: Arghya Rakshit, Aranya Sen

item.title: Stability of optimal transport maps and second variation of the 2-Monge-Kantorovich distance
item.description: arXiv:2605.24232v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish several quantitative stability estimates for optimal transport maps between non-degenerate densities on uniformly convex domains for the quadratic cost. Under H\"older regularity assumptions, we prove Lipschitz $L^{2}$ (respectively $C^{0,\alpha}$) stability estimates for optimal transport maps in terms of the $2$-Monge--Kantorovich distance (respectively $L^{p}$ distances) between pairs of source and target densities. When the continuity assumption is removed, we obtain a Lipschitz $L^{2}$ stability estimate for the Brenier potentials in terms of the $L^{2}$ distance between the source and target densities. The proofs rely on a precise characterization of the linear response of the Brenier potential along smooth interpolations of the data, obtained by linearizing the Monge--Amp\`ere equation in divergence form. As a further application of this approach, we derive an explicit formula for the second variation of the quadratic Monge--Kantorovich distance.
item.dc:creator: F. -U. Caja-Lopez, Matias G. Delgadino, Jun Kitagawa

item.title: Resonant Microstructures as Dirac-type Sources for Acoustic Wave Control
item.description: arXiv:2605.25978v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study finite-time acoustic wave tracking using effective interior Dirac-type actuators generated by clusters of subwavelength resonant bubbles driven from exterior transducers. Starting from a time-domain point-interaction approximation, the full scattering problem is reduced to a finite-dimensional delayed system of interacting retarded monopoles. After localization to a bounded observation domain, we formulate the tracking problem on a prescribed finite-dimensional Dirichlet spectral subspace. At the ideal level, a full-rank spatial coupling condition yields exact tracking of arbitrary sufficiently smooth compatible trajectories in this subspace by interior point sources. These ideal actuators are realized using small, high-contrast bubbles, whose Laplace-domain transfer operator encodes the Minnaert resonances and collective attenuation. The principal mode of each cluster is isolated by the Perron--Frobenius structure and the intra-cluster spectral gap. Clusters tuned to the same band are then treated as a collective resonant block. The selected Dirichlet bands are matched with the corresponding Minnaert bands. For prescribed slowly time-modulated resonant pressure profiles, with sufficiently flat initialization, we construct causal exterior controls and obtain a quantitative tracking estimate on every fixed time interval $[0,T]$. In contrast, on frequency ranges uniformly separated from the Minnaert resonances, the actuator gain is $O(\varepsilon)$ and the corresponding realization cost is asymptotically unbounded as $\varepsilon \ll 1$, $\varepsilon$ being the maximum radius of the bubbles. Thus the Minnaert resonances convert accessible exterior excitations into robust effective interior controls.
item.dc:creator: Arpan Mukherjee, Mourad Sini

item.title: The quantitative isoperimetric inequality: A calibration argument
item.description: arXiv:2606.17172v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a short proof of the quantitative isoperimetric inequality. Our argument is based on a notion of quantitative calibrations which induce a natural distance controlling both the Fraenkel asymmetry and the tilt excess. The proof of our key result which can be viewed as a nonlinear, geometric version of Fuglede's result in $BV$ is direct and self-contained. In particular, we do not make any use of regularity theory for almost minimizers.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Hensel, Tim Laux

item.title: An inverse free boundary problem
item.description: arXiv:2608.21153v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study inverse problems for the elliptic and parabolic obstacle problems from boundary measurements. For the classical elliptic obstacle problem with strictly superharmonic obstacle function, we show that the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map admits a one-sided linearization at every boundary datum lying strictly above the obstacle. The linearized map is the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for a rough Dirichlet problem on the a priori unknown non-contact set. We show that these linearized Cauchy data uniquely determine the non-contact set up to set of Sobolev $2$-capacity zero and consequently determine the obstacle. Our result applies to the inverse problem for a parabolic obstacle problem where both the coefficient and the obstacle function are time-independent by reducing to the elliptic inverse problem.
item.dc:creator: C\u{a}t\u{a}lin I. C\^{a}rstea, Matti Lassas, Jinpeng Lu, Lauri Oksanen, Ziyao Zhao

item.title: The scattering matrix for the p-form Laplacian on asymptotically conic manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2608.22984v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Hodge decomposition at infinity gives rise to distinct tangential scattering channels for differential forms on asymptotically conic manifolds. We construct co-closed generalized eigenforms for the Hodge Laplacian on $p$-forms in dimension $n\geq 3$ and analyze the resulting Bessel and Hankel systems. From these we determine the scattering matrix modulo smoothing operators, identifying it as a Fourier integral operator associated to the time $\pi$ geodesic flow and whose principal symbol encodes fibre-wise parallel transport with respect to the Levi-Civita connection on differential forms. In this setting this lifts the main result of Melrose and Zworski in [24] to differential forms and identifies additional scattering phase. The construction also yields a spectral representation in the co-closed sector, including a Stone-type formula and a functional calculus. In dimension $3$ and degree $p=1$, this framework describes divergence-free fields and thus the electric-field component of Maxwell's equations.
item.dc:creator: Nelia Charalambous, Alden Waters

item.title: Fastest-Species Selection in Critical Multispecies Competition-Diffusion Systems via an Entropy Approach
item.description: arXiv:2608.24253v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study an $N$-species competition--diffusion system with a common competition term, for which the associated ODE system admits infinitely many equilibria. For $N=2$, Alfaro and Xiao \cite{AlfaroXiao2023} studied the long-time behavior of solutions with compactly supported initial data by constructing precise super- and sub-solutions. For $N \geq 3$, the absence of a comparison principle for the entire system presents a major difficulty. Using a weighted entropy method, we prove that every bounded nonnegative traveling profile connecting nonzero equilibria is constant, without imposing any monotonicity assumption. For nontrivial compactly supported initial populations, we further show that the species with the strictly largest Fisher-KPP speed excludes all slower species and spreads at its scalar Fisher-KPP speed. Finally, we establish heat-type lower bounds for the slower species, revealing a bump phenomenon despite their uniform extinction.
item.dc:creator: Haozhe Shu, Dongyuan Xiao

item.title: A counterexample to Kenig's conjecture for the Laplace double-layer operator
item.description: arXiv:2609.07947v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We disprove Kenig's 1994 spectral-radius conjecture for the double-layer operator in every dimension $d\ge2$. For every $t>1/2$ sufficiently close to $1/2$, we construct a bounded simply connected Lipschitz domain with connected boundary such that the double-layer operator on $L^2$ with respect to the surface measure has $\pm \mathrm{i} t$ in its Fredholm essential spectrum. In particular, the essential spectral radius is greater than $1/2$. In the plane, the boundary may be chosen differentiable everywhere and smooth away from a single point. Our planar construction develops a refinement mechanism that produces unbounded growth of adjoint resolvent solutions with fixed forcing while keeping the graph slopes uniformly bounded. A closed recursion for the density and its image under an auxiliary singular integral reduces the growth estimate to a certified inequality for Hermitian $2\times2$ matrices. The certificate uses continuous estimates, exact rational arithmetic and rigorous interval enclosures. Localisation and rescaled graph insertions then produce a weakly null sequence of normalised approximate eigenvectors for the adjoint double-layer operator on one bounded boundary. A compact intertwining relation on Cartesian products of the planar domain with cubes gives the higher-dimensional examples without changing the spectral parameter.
item.dc:creator: Matthew J. Colbrook, Siavash Sadeghi

item.title: Dimension-dependent symmetry breaking in a diffusive nonlocal interaction model
item.description: arXiv:2609.16978v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the equilibrium structure and long-time behavior of a nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation with diffusion and nonlocal interactions generated by squared simplex volumes. For $1\leq n<d$, the stationary states are isotropic Gaussian measures, and every solution converges to the equilibrium determined by its conserved mean. At $n=d$, the free energy fixes only the covariance determinant, allowing a continuum of anisotropic Gaussian equilibria when $d\geq2$. We establish global well-posedness for arbitrary initial probability measures with finite second moment, identify stationary states with the global minimizers of the free energy, and prove convergence in quadratic Wasserstein distance with explicit exponential rates.
item.dc:creator: Dohyun Kim, Hansol Park, Woojoo Shim

item.title: Multidimensional fractional material derivative: measure-valued solutions and probabilistic properties
item.description: arXiv:2609.20060v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze a nonlocal operator in space and time, called the multidimensional fractional material derivative. We derive its pointwise representation, which allows us to study its other properties. We define an inverse operator, called fractional material integral, and derive its pointwise representation. Furthermore, we analyze a class of linear partial differential equations, which corresponds to deterministic descriptions of the scaling limits of multidimensional L\'evy walks, in which transport is driven by a multidimensional fractional material derivative with a speed vector integrated with respect to a suitable probability measure and a distributional source term. Using Fourier-Laplace transform techniques and a direct convolution-kernel construction, we prove the existence and uniqueness of exponentially integrable measure solutions for measure data. Moreover, we identify a necessary and sufficient condition on the source term for conservation of unit mass and provide separate sufficient conditions for non-negativity and weak convergence to $\delta_0$. We also prove weak continuity and self-similarity of the kernel and continuous dependence on the directional distribution.
item.dc:creator: Hubert Woszczek

item.title: Existence and non-existence of extremal functions for inequalities of Bliss-Moser type
item.description: arXiv:2609.23251v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a concentration--compactness theory for a one-dimensional singular Moser-type functional with logarithmic weight function $$\sup\limits_{v\in E }\int_0^1 e^{\left(\log\frac{e}{s}+\gamma\log\log\frac{e}{s}\right)\frac{v^2(s)}{s}}ds<\infty,~\gamma\in[0,1],$$ where $$E:= \left\{u \in H^{1}(0, 1): u(0) = 0, \int_0^1 |u'|^2dx=1\right\}.$$ In particular, we prove compactness for all normalized sequences in the subcritical range $\gamma<1$, thereby resolving an open problem proposed in [J. M. do \'{O}, B. Ruf and P. Ubilla, CVPDE 2023]. We also study the critical Bliss-Moser inequality: \begin{equation}\nonumber \sup\limits_{v\in E }I^c(v)< +\infty,\quad I^c(v)=\int_0^1 e^{\left(\log\frac{e}{s}+\log\log\frac{e}{s}+cs\right)\frac{v^2(s)}{s}}ds. \end{equation} For any $c\in(-\infty,+\infty)$, we determine the sharp concentration level $$\sup_{v_j\in E,v_j~\text{is~NCS}}\limsup\limits_{j\to\infty} I^c(v_j)=1+e^2,$$ and obtain explicit sufficient conditions for attainability under $c>c^*$ and non-attainability under $c<-c_*$. This results describe how linear perturbations govern the transition between compactness, concentration, and attainability at the critical level.
item.dc:creator: Yanyan Guo, Huxiao Luo, Bernhard Ruf

item.title: Global well-posedness and scattering for the three-dimensional defocusing cubic Schr\"odinger equation in $H^s$, $s>\frac{1}{2}$
item.description: arXiv:2609.24830v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove global well-posedness and scattering for the three-dimensional defocusing cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with arbitrary initial data in $H^s(\R^3)$, $s>\frac{1}{2}$, without radial symmetry. The proof combines the $I$-method with long-time $L^2_{t,x}$ bounds for products of frequency-localized components of the nonlinear solution. The key high--low estimate follows from a directional interaction identity pairing high-frequency mass with low-frequency energy, together with an induction on frequency.
item.dc:creator: Qingtang Su, Zehua Zhao

item.title: Blow-up for a semilinear Tricomi equation in the oscillatory regime at the critical Strauss-type exponent
item.description: arXiv:2609.28389v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study finite-time blow-up for a semilinear shifted Tricomi equation with decreasing propagation speed and an oscillatory scale-invariant mass. We focus on the Strauss-type critical regime and prove that every weak solution with finite speed of propagation, arising from nonnegative nontrivial energy data satisfying a suitable localization condition, blows up in finite time. For sufficiently small initial data, we also obtain the corresponding critical exponential upper bound for the lifespan. The proof relies on a positive self-similar solution of the homogeneous adjoint equation represented by the Gauss hypergeometric function. Combined with a previously established lower bound for the nonlinear term and new estimates adapted to the critical case, this construction reduces the PDE problem to a nonlinear differential inequality. An ODE comparison argument then yields both finite-time blow-up and the lifespan estimate.
item.dc:creator: Diego Marcon, Wanderley Nunes do Nascimento, Matheus C. Santos

item.title: Global well-posedness of defocusing cubic NLS in $M^{\infty,1}(\mathbb{R})$
item.description: arXiv:2609.29147v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove global well-posedness of the one-dimensional defocusing cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation in the modulation space $M^{\infty,1}(\mathbb{R})$. This space imposes no spatial decay and contains $C_b^2(\mathbb{R})$ as well as all absolutely convergent sums of plane waves. The result applies to arbitrary data in this space, including large smooth quasiperiodic profiles and their localized perturbations. The proof constructs a nonnegative density satisfying a local conservation law from forward Weyl ratios, which are defined through half-line square-integrable solutions of the associated spectral problem. A suitable nonlinear combination of localized integrals of this density controls the modulation norm. Finally, choosing the spatial localization scale and NLS scaling in a coordinated way makes the accumulated boundary flux small enough to continue every mild solution globally.
item.dc:creator: Friedrich Klaus

item.title: On the Cauchy problem for the Tzitz\'{e}ica equation: Soliton resolution conjecture and asymptotic analysis
item.description: arXiv:2609.30858v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the soliton resolution conjecture for the Tzitz\'eica equation, which is an important integrable model arising in affine differential geometry and characterizing proper affine spheres. Recently, Huang, Wang and Zhu (Math. Ann. \textbf{395}, 18 (2026)) reported the long-time asymptotic result for the Tzitz\'eica equation with purely continuous spectrum. Inspired by their work, we carry out a full asymptotic analysis of the Tzitz\'eica equation. Compared with the previous work, by developing the $\bar{\partial}$-nonlinear steepest descent method, we reveal that the solutions of the Tzitz\'eica equation exhibits three different asymptotic regions depending on $\xi:=x/t$. For the region $\xi\in(-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)$, where there are no stationary phase points, we rigorously prove that the solution satisfies $u(x,t)=O_\xi(t^{-1})$ for $\xi\ge1$ and $u(x,t)=2\pi i+O_\xi(t^{-1})$ for $\xi\le-1$. In the region $\xi\in(-1,1)$, the phase function $\theta(z)$ has two stationary phase points. The corresponding asymptotic approximations can be characterized with an $N$-soliton solution as well as an interaction term between soliton solutions and the dispersion term with a residual error of order $O(t^{-3/4+b_K})$ with $0\le b_K<1/4$. In the transition regions $\{(x,t):1-\varepsilon<|\xi|<1\}$, the corresponding asymptotic approximation can be characterized by the dispersion term with a residual error of order $O(t^{-3/4+b_\varepsilon})$ where $0\le b_\varepsilon<1/4$. Our results provide a rigorous analysis of the long-time asymptotic behavior of solutions of the Tzitz\'eica equation in different regions and confirm the soliton resolution conjecture for the Tzitz\'eica equation.
item.dc:creator: Shou-Fu Tian, Jia-Fu Tong

item.title: Stability of 3D Stratified Plane Couette Flow: A New Lift-up Mechanism and Potential Vorticity
item.description: arXiv:2609.33960v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Since the pioneering work of Taylor and Goldstein in 1931 laid the foundation for the study of parallel stratified shear flows, non-parallel configurations have received comparatively little attention. We study the stability of the 3D Boussinesq system near the plane Couette flow $V^*=(y,0,0)$ under the vertically stratified background $\eta^*=\alpha z$. The shear and stratification directions are perpendicular. This geometry produces two structural effects that are absent in the parallel configuration: an additional nonlocal coupling in the non-zero-mode system, which obstructs a directly useful symmetrization, and a wave-shear coupled lift-up mechanism for the zero modes. The $L^p$ transient growth due to the lift-up effect can be suppressed either by sufficiently strong stratification (for $p>2$) or under suitable assumptions on the initial data (for $p\geq 2$). To study the nonzero-mode system, we introduce a reformulation based on the linearized potential vorticity (PV), a fundamental quantity in geophysical fluid dynamics, to recover a better energy structure.
