We establish the inviscid damping of $u_{1,\neq}$ and $u_{2,\neq}$. We further apply the linearized PV formulation to study the linear stability of the tilted Couette flow. Finally, we use this formulation to prove the nonlinear stability for perturbations on $\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$.
item.dc:creator: Yiting Yao

item.title: Global H\"older estimates for linearized Monge-Amp\`ere equations in divergence form with applications to dual semigeostrophic equations and periodic homogenization
item.description: arXiv:2610.02071v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish interior and global H\"older estimates for linearized Monge-Amp\`ere equations in divergence form in all dimensions $n\geq 3$, when the Hessian determinant of the convex Monge-Amp\`ere potential is bounded above and below by positive constants and the vector field on the right-hand side is bounded. The estimates use the $L^p$ norm of the solution for any $p>1$. A key ingredient is an $L^1$ estimate, with appropriate decay rates, for the gradient of the Green's function of the linearized Monge-Amp\`ere operator in small sections, uniform with respect to the pole. As applications, we obtain uniform H\"older estimates for the time derivatives of the primal and dual potentials in the three-dimensional periodic dual semigeostrophic system when the initial density is bounded away from zero and infinity, and establish a linear convergence rate for periodic homogenization of the Monge-Amp\`ere equation.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Cui, Chong Gu, Nam Q. Le, Ling Wang, Bin Zhou

item.title: Sharp Truncated Difference Estimates for Nonlocal Nonconvex Functionals Defined by Superlevel Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.04259v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $N\in\mathbb N$ and $p\in[1,\infty)$. In this article, we consider a family $\{\Phi_{\lambda,p}^{\gamma}\}_{\lambda\in(0,\infty)}$ of nonlocal nonconvex functionals with a real parameter $\gamma$ and establish two truncated difference estimates bounded by these functionals with the sharp range of $\gamma$; that is, for any $\gamma\in(-\infty,-1]$, any $\lambda\in(0,\infty)$, any cube $Q\subset\mathbb R^N$, and any measurable function $g:Q\to\mathbb R$, \begin{align*} &\int_Q\int_Q\left[\frac{|g(x)-g(y)|-\lambda|x-y|^{1+\gamma/p}}{\ell(Q)^{1+\gamma/p}}\right]_+^p\,dx\,dy\\ &\quad\lesssim \lambda^p\mathop{\int_Q\int_Q}\limits_{\frac{|g(x)-g(y)|}{|x-y|^{1+\gamma/p}}>\lambda}\left[\frac{|x-y|}{\ell(Q)}\right]^{\gamma-N}\,dx\,dy=:\frac{\Phi_{\lambda,p}^{\gamma}(g;Q)}{\ell(Q)^{\gamma-N}}, \end{align*} where the implicit positive constant depends only on $N$, $p$, and $\gamma$. For $\gamma\in(0,\infty)$, the above estimate holds with the left-most integrand replaced by $\frac{\min\{|g(x)-g(y)|^p,\lambda^p|x-y|^{p+\gamma}\}}{\ell(Q)^{p+\gamma}}$. As applications, these estimates yield related nonlocal Poincar\'e inequalities with the sharp range of $\gamma$, and also recover the known $\Gamma$-liminf lower bounds and characterizations of Sobolev and BV spaces in terms of the liminf of the functionals $\{\Phi^\gamma_{\lambda,p}\}_{\lambda\in(0,\infty)}$ for all $\gamma\in\mathbb{R}\setminus(-1,0]$. We investigate further applications to compactness and variational problems as well as a new VMO criterion. Inspired by a recent work of R. L. Frank, we develop an elementary approach based on dyadic iteration of truncated differences along line segments, which allows us to treat the aforementioned problems in a unified way.
item.dc:creator: Feng Dai, Dachun Yang, Wen Yuan, Yirui Zhao

item.title: Low Mach number limit of the full Navier-Stokes equations with no-slip boundary conditions and large temperature variations
item.description: arXiv:2610.06567v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we rigorously justify the low Mach number limit of the full compressible Navier-Stokes equations in a three-dimensional smooth bounded domain, subject to the no-slip boundary condition for the velocity and well-prepared initial data. In the presence of heat conduction and large temperature variations, we establish the uniform estimates for strong solutions on a time interval independent of the Mach number by constructing an energy functional in a Sobolev framework. The no-slip boundary condition cannot provide the vorticity boundary relation used in the slip-boundary setting. To overcome this difficulty, a divergence-free Stokes lifting of the boundary trace for the time derivative of the modified velocity is employed to define a test function vanishing on the boundary, which enables the transfer of a priori estimates from the velocity to the temperature.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyu Gu, Song Jiang, Qiangchang Ju, Yaobin Ou

item.title: Convexity preservation for first-order nonlinear evolution equations with Neumann-type boundary conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.11509v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study preservation of spatial convexity for viscosity solutions of first order Hamilton-Jacobi evolution equations with Neumann-type boundary conditions in bounded convex domains. Under a monotonicity assumption on the Hamiltonian in the outward normal direction, every viscosity supersolution of the Neumann problem is also a state-constraint supersolution. This reduces the boundary difficulty to a state-constraint problem and enables us to prove convexity preservation via the convex-envelope argument established by Alvarez, Lasry and Lions (1997). We also obtain propagation estimates for semiconvexity and strong convexity under similar structural assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Daowen Lin, Qing Liu

item.title: Existence and uniqueness of viscous-dispersive shock profiles for the Navier-Stokes-Fourier-Korteweg system
item.description: arXiv:2610.16874v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the existence and uniqueness, up to translation, of monotone viscous-dispersive shock profiles for the one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier-Korteweg system, provided the two end states satisfy the Rankine-Hugoniot and Lax entropy conditions and the shock strength is small. Taking the shock strength as a singular perturbation parameter, we reduce the profile equations by Fenichel's geometric singular perturbation theory to a scalar equation on a slow manifold and obtain the profile as a heteroclinic orbit. We also give pointwise estimates of the profiles and their derivatives up to fourth order, with explicit leading-order terms for the first derivatives.
item.dc:creator: Sungho Han

item.title: What remains when integrability fails? Mathematical structure in the K(m,m) compacton equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.17489v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Peter Lax's 1968 discovery that certain nonlinear wave equations possess operator pairs (Lax pairs) opened the theory of completely integrable systems, yielding exact solutions, infinite conservation hierarchies, and perfectly elastic soliton collisions. When a nonlinear dispersive equation is provably non-integrable (admitting no Lax pair and only finitely many conservation laws), what mathematical structure governs its dynamics? The K(m,m) compacton equations, u_t + (u^m)_x + (u^m)_{xxx} = 0 for m >= 2, provide a testing ground: they support traveling waves with compact support, yet fail every known integrability test. We prove universal algebraic formulas determining the shape, width, and speed of every K(m,m) compacton. We develop a constraint-deficit mechanism explaining how the five independent conservation laws constrain emergent amplitudes and suppress the fundamental Fourier mode of the collision debris, while higher radiation modes remain unconstrained. The mechanism's conclusions rest on explicit hypotheses supported by numerical evidence. A phase-plane analysis reveals the compacton as a singular limit of smooth solitary waves through simultaneous regularity loss and support compactification. These results delineate intermediate territory between integrable order and generic nonlinear dynamics, organized by scaling universality and by the constraint deficit of a finite conservation structure.
item.dc:creator: James M. Hyman

item.title: Global well-posedness of the periodic Majda-Biello systems in the resonant case
item.description: arXiv:2610.22260v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for the following Majda-Biello system in the resonant case $\alpha \in (0,4]\setminus\{1\}$ on the periodic domain $\mathbb{T}$. \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{rcl} u_{t} + u_{xxx} & = & - v v_x, v_{t} + \alpha v_{xxx} & = & - (uv)_{x}, (u,v)|_{t=0} & = & (u_0,v_0), \end{array} \right. \quad x \in \mathbb{T}, \, t \in \mathbb{R}. \] Here, the initial data $u_0$ and $v_0$ live in the Sobolev space $H^{s}(\mathbb{T})$ and $u_0$ has zero mean over $\mathbb{T}$. We establish the optimal global well-posedness for the above system when $s\geq \min\{1, s_\alpha+\}$, where $s_\alpha$ is a constant depending only on $\alpha$, and $s_\alpha = \frac12$ for almost every $\alpha \in (0,4]\setminus\{1\}$. These indices match the sharp ones in the local theory obtained by Oh (Int. Math. Res. Not., 18:3516-3556, 2009). The main novelty of our proof is to introduce a third modified energy in the I-method by performing a partial correction to the second modified energy around the resonant region. This partial correction avoids the singularity in the full correction, and therefore makes it possible to pointwise bound the quintilinear multipliers arising in the time derivative of the third modified energy. Another feature in our proof is the combination of the Diophantine approximation theory with the sparsity of nearly resonant frequency pairs on the periodic lattice to obtain the key quadrilinear and quintilinear estimates, leading to an almost conservation law sufficient for the global iteration.
item.dc:creator: Ke Wang, Xin Yang

item.title: Memory effects in the homogenization of a viscous fluid containing small elastic particles
item.description: arXiv:2610.23819v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work deals with a fluid-structure interaction problem involving an incompressible viscous fluid and a periodic array of tiny elastic inclusions in a three-dimensional domain. We focus on a critical regime where the volume fraction of the inclusions tends to zero, but their density and stiffness are scaled so that they still influence the macroscopic behavior. The asymptotic regime depends on the parameter $\gamma=\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}r_\varepsilon/\varepsilon^3\in [0,+\infty]$, where $\varepsilon$ is the period and $r_\varepsilon$ the inclusion size. For $\gamma=0$ the solid and fluid equations uncouple in the limit. For $\gamma\in (0,+\infty]$, we show that the macroscopic fluid velocity satisfies a Stokes system with memory: the standard Stokes equations are augmented by convolution-in-time terms arising from the elastic vibrations of the inclusions. The existence of the convolution kernels is established for both $\gamma\in(0,+\infty)$ and $\gamma=\infty$ using semigroup theory. For $\gamma=\infty$ the microscopic problem reduces to a purely conservative elastodynamic equation and the kernels can be computed explicitly via spectral decomposition. They are oscillatory and almost-periodic in time, yielding a persistent, non-decaying memory. For $\gamma\in(0,+\infty)$ the microscopic elastodynamic equation is coupled to a local Stokes problem, whose viscous dissipation yields memory kernels that decay to zero at infinity.
item.dc:creator: Juan Casado-D\'iaz, Antonio Rafael Hormigo-Molina

item.title: Equivalence of local weak and Benjamini--Schramm formulations of Berry's random wave model
item.description: arXiv:2305.14906v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Berry's random wave model predicts that high-energy eigenfunctions of classically chaotic systems can be modeled locally, at the wavelength scale, by the Gaussian monochromatic random wave. Several rigorous formulations of this prediction have been proposed. We prove the equivalence of two such formulations on a closed manifold: local weak limits and Benjamini--Schramm convergence of manifolds decorated by eigenfunctions. The latter considers pointed manifolds equipped with a smooth function, up to isometry, without recording local orthonormal coordinates. The key step is to recover the unaveraged local function law from its orthogonal average using translation invariance and the ergodicity of the random wave. Finally, either formulation implies strong inverse localization, allowing high-energy eigenfunctions to approximate arbitrary solutions of the Euclidean Helmholtz equation, with applications to their nodal sets.
item.dc:creator: Alba Garc\'ia-Ruiz

item.title: Sharp Quartic Pinching for the Mean Curvature Flow in the Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2408.08022v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a sharp quartic curvature pinching for the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{S}^{n+m}$, $m\ge2$, which generalises Pu's work on the convergence of submanifolds in $\mathbb{S}^{n+m}$ to a round point. Using a blow up argument, we prove a codimension and a cylindrical estimate, where in regions of high curvature, the submanifold becomes approximately codimension one, quantitatively, and is weakly convex and moves by translation or is a self shrinker. With a decay estimate, the rescaling converges smoothly to a totally geodesic limit in infinite time, without using Stampacchia iteration or integral analysis.
item.dc:creator: Artemis A. Vogiatzi

item.title: The Restricted Three-Body Problem as a Perturbed Duffing Equation
item.description: arXiv:2505.07104v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper investigates the restricted circular planar three-body problem. We prove that for every negative Jacobi constant of sufficiently large magnitude, the surface of unperturbed parabolic solutions breaks to induce homoclinic tangles for all but at most finitely many mass ratios of primaries. Our approach relies on reformulating the restricted three-body problem as a perturbed Duffing equation by introducing new coordinate transformations. This enables us to capture the order of the singularities involved through a renormalized Duffing Hamiltonian structure, to derive the existence and analytic dependence of the invariant manifolds on the mass ratio of the primaries, and to evaluate the Poincar\'e-Melnikov integral directly through the explicit homoclinic solution of the unperturbed Duffing equation. Compared to existing works, our proof is significantly simpler and more direct. Moreover, the paper is self-contained: we do not rely on McGehee's analysis in \cite{Mc} to justify the applicability of the Poincar\'e-Melnikov method.
item.dc:creator: Rongchang Liu, Qiudong Wang

item.title: Quantitative convergence for displacement monotone Mean Field Games of control
item.description: arXiv:2507.17014v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we establish quantitative convergence results for both open and closed-loop Nash equilibria of N-player stochastic differential games in the setting of Mean Field Games of Controls (MFGC), a class of models where interactions among agents occur through both states and controls. Our analysis covers a general class of non-separable Hamiltonians satisfying a displacement monotonicity condition, along with mild regularity and growth conditions at infinity. A major novelty of our work is the rigorous treatment of a nontrivial fixed-point problem on a space of measures, which arises naturally in the MFGC formulation. Unlike prior works that either restrict to separable Hamiltonians - rendering the fixed-point map trivial - or assume convergence or regularity properties of the fixed point map, we develop a detailed structural analysis of this equation and its N-player analogue. This leads to new regularity results for the fixed-point maps and, in turn, to quantitative convergence of open-loop equilibria. We further derive sharp a priori estimates for the N-player Nash system, enabling us to control the discrepancy between open and closed-loop strategies, and thus to conclude the convergence of closed-loop equilibria. Our framework also accommodates common noise in a natural way.
item.dc:creator: Joe Jackson, Alp\'ar R. M\'esz\'aros

item.title: Levi Flat Structures via Structure Sheaves: Differential Complexes, Convexity, and Global Solvability
item.description: arXiv:2507.18341v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper investigates Levi flat structures from the perspective of structure sheaves. We employ formal integrability to construct a class of differential complexes, thereby providing a resolution of the structure sheaf and a global realization of the Treves complex. Drawing inspiration from Morse theory and Grauert's convexity, we introduce notions of convexity and positivity that fully exploit Levi flatness, which yield global exactness of the differential complex and Sobolev regularity in the compact case. As applications, we establish the global solvability of the Treves complex for Levi flat structures, together with results on singular cohomology and the extension problem for canonical forms in the elliptic case.
item.dc:creator: Qingchun Ji, Jun Yao

item.title: Ancient Gauss curvature flows of bounded width
item.description: arXiv:2510.05614v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we construct a pancake-like ancient compact solution with flat sides to the Gauss curvature flow, contained in a slab. Also, we construct sausage-like ancient compact solutions to the $\alpha$-Gauss curvature flow with $\alpha >\frac{1}{2}$, asymptotic to a round cylinder.
item.dc:creator: Beomjun Choi, Kyeongsu Choi, Dongjun Noh

item.title: Spectrum of the wave equation with Dirac damping on a compact star graph
item.description: arXiv:2510.09829v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the wave equation with a distributional Dirac damping and Dirichlet boundary conditions on a compact interval. It is shown that the spectrum of the corresponding wave operator is fully determined by zeroes of an entire function. Consequently, a considerable change of spectral properties is shown for certain critical values of the damping parameter. We also derive a definitive criterion for the Riesz basis property of the root vectors for an arbitrary placement of a complex-valued Dirac damping. Finally, we consider a generalisation of the problem for compact star graphs and provide insight into the essence of the critical damping constant.
item.dc:creator: Mikul\'a\v{s} Ku\v{c}era

item.title: Distance Functions, Curvature and Topology
item.description: arXiv:2602.17629v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We discuss some properties of the distance functions on Riemannian manifolds and we relate their behavior to the geometry of the manifolds. This leads to alternative proofs of some "classical" theorems connecting curvature and topology.
item.dc:creator: Carlo Mantegazza, Francesca Oronzio

item.title: Galerkin Approximation of the Fractional Sobolev Constant
item.description: arXiv:2605.13347v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish sharp estimates for the discrete optimal constant of the fractional Sobolev inequality in dimension $N\geq 1$, with fractional exponent $s\in (0,\min\{1,N/2\})$. The convergence rates that we establish take place for the Galerkin approximation with piecewise linear elements, when the problem is posed in the unit ball, for which we employ a quasi-uniform and regular mesh. Since the infimum defining the fractional Sobolev constant is not attained on bounded domains, these estimates quantify how far a piecewise affine mesh of size $h$ can resolve the concentration of the optimizers: the discrete minimizers are close to bubbles concentrated at the scale $h^{2(2-s)/(N+4(1-s))}$, and the energy gap is exactly of order $h^{2(2-s)(N-2s)/(N+4(1-s))}$.
item.dc:creator: Andreea Dima, Liviu I. Ignat

item.title: Bregman-projected mirror methods for regularized stationary mean-field games
item.description: arXiv:2606.19611v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop and analyze a Bregman-projected mirror iteration for low-order regularizations of stationary mean-field game (MFG) systems in their natural Banach space setting. For separable Hamiltonians of the form $H(x,p,m)=H_0(x,p)-g(m)$, with quadratic or super-quadratic Hamiltonian growth and linear or super-linear density couplings, we formulate a low-order $\bar\gamma$-Laplacian regularization of the stationary MFG system as a variational inequality on $L^{\bar\beta}(\mathbb T^d)\times W^{1,\bar\gamma}(\mathbb T^d)$. To approximate solutions of this regularized variational inequality, we introduce a Bregman geometry matched to the mixed Lebesgue-Sobolev exponents of the problem and analyze the exact constrained one-step mirror iteration and a frozen two-step variant. Under quantitative monotonicity of the coupling, both exact iterations converge strongly to the unique solution of the regularized variational inequality for each fixed $\varepsilon>0$, under natural summability conditions on the step sizes. Along weakly convergent vanishing-regularization sequences, we also prove strong convergence in the full product space. Numerical experiments in one and two dimensions show first-order accuracy on manufactured solutions and weak dependence of outer iteration counts on the tested grids. At matched effective step sizes, the frozen two-step and one-step implementations agree up to inner-solve accuracy, while the latter requires fewer mirror solves.
item.dc:creator: Hussain Al Abdulaziz, Yuri Ashrafyan, Yeva Gevorgyan, Diogo Gomes

item.title: Searching Schemes With $p$-Adic Neumann Boundary Value Problems
item.description: arXiv:2609.27751v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Firstly, for branched covering maps $f\colon Y\to X$ between smooth, separated schemes of finite type over the integral ring $O_K$ of a non-archimedean local field $K$, the ramification divisor is found to coincide with the divisor of the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the Radon measure associated with an algebraic differential form on $Y$ against the pullback measure of one on $X$, both taking Borel sets of the space $Y(O_K)$ of $O_K$-rational points of $Y$ as input values. Secondly, the ultracontractivity of semigroups generated by Laplacian integral operators having a geodetic-distance-power kernel function is proven, using heat kernel estimates for ultrametric operators on $p$-adic balls. Thirdly, a series of $p$-adic Neumann Boundary Value Problems, depending on algebraic and pluricanonical differential forms with poles on spaces $X(O_K)$ coming from schemes is formulated and solved, extending previous work of the author. These results are then used to solve reconstruction problems on schemes: the divisor of a pluricanonical form with poles with at worst log-terminal singularities, as well as Weierstrass points of projective algebraic curves can be reconstructed via repeatedly finding weak solutions of $p$-adic Neumann Boundary Value Problems.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Erik Bradley

item.title: Recovering a Riemannian manifold from minimal surface areas
item.description: arXiv:2610.13405v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the recovery of a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold from the areas of minimal surfaces. We show that areas of minimal surfaces determine the metric on manifolds foliated by minimal surfaces, up to boundary-fixing isometry. This resolves the conjecture on boundary rigidity for least-area data in an exterior formulation, even without topological restrictions on the minimal surfaces.
